quizItems.scenario: Smoke is banking down the hallway ceiling but visibility at floor level is still clear.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Stay low and continue moving toward the search objective.
Pause briefly to reassess, then continue low.
Retreat fully and wait for conditions to improve.
Stand upright to move faster through the hallway.

quizItems.rationale: Banking smoke with clear floor-level visibility is still passable low; standing upright into the smoke layer is the worst choice.

quizItems.scenario: This corridor connects four rooms and is the only path to the stairwell from this side of the floor.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Keep this hallway clear and ventilated before focusing on side rooms.
Search a side room first, then return to the hallway.
Treat it as equal priority to any single room.
Let smoke bank here while fully clearing one room first.

quizItems.rationale: A blocked single-path corridor traps every room behind it; protecting it outranks searching any one adjoining room first.

quizItems.scenario: The room is clear, but a baby monitor on the shelf is powered on and transmitting static.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Treat it as evidence of an infant nearby and prioritize nearby bedrooms.
Note it and continue the standard search order.
Mark the room cleared and move on.
Disregard it as an irrelevant object.

quizItems.rationale: A powered baby monitor strongly implies a child is present somewhere nearby; disregarding it is the worst read of the evidence.

quizItems.scenario: The closet door is slightly ajar and you notice small shoes just inside.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Check inside -- children sometimes hide in closets during a fire.
Glance in from the doorway without physically checking.
Note the shoes and move on.
Skip the closet entirely since it's a small space.

quizItems.rationale: Closets are a common hiding spot for frightened children; a quick but thorough check is low-cost and high-value, skipping it entirely is worst.

quizItems.scenario: The bathroom door is locked from the inside. You hear coughing.
quizItems.question: Rank these actions best to worst.

options.text: Force entry immediately -- an audible occupant is an active rescue.
Knock and wait for a response before forcing entry.
Look for a key elsewhere in the unit first.
Move on and note it as 'occupied, locked' for later.

quizItems.rationale: Coughing means a live, distressed occupant; moving on without acting is the worst option by far.
